title: Valued-field description of admissible-modification stalks
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair with $I$ finitely generated, $A'=\widehat A$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $U=X\setminus V(I)$, $X'=\operatorname{Spec}A'$ and $U'=X'\times_XU$ [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $F$ be a torsion abelian sheaf on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $F'$ its inverse image on $U'_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Use the common limit topos $\mathcal T$ of the closed fibres of the admissible blowups and the sheaves $L^q_F,L^q_{F'}$ defined by the colimits of restricted higher direct images in [lem-per-admissible-modification-cohomology-presentation]. Its geometric points admit a conservative subfamily with the following property. For each point $t$ in that subfamily there are nontrivially valued fields $K_t\hookrightarrow K'_t$, both henselian for their valuation rings [def-trf-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], such that the inclusion induces the valuation topology on $K_t$ and has dense image in $K'_t$. There is a torsion abelian etale sheaf $G_t$ on $\operatorname{Spec}K_t$ and, simultaneously for every $q\geq0$, natural identifications
$$(L^q_F)_t\cong H^q((\operatorname{Spec}K_t)_{\mathrm{et}},G_t),\qquad (L^q_{F'})_t\cong H^q((\operatorname{Spec}K'_t)_{\mathrm{et}},G_t|_{K'_t}).$$
They identify the stalk of the exchange map $L^q_F\to L^q_{F'}$ with the canonical field-extension pullback on these groups [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. A valuation topology has neighbourhoods of zero given by the inequalities $v(x)>\gamma$ in an ordered value group; dense means that each nonempty open ball meets the subfield. No isomorphism on these cohomology groups is asserted.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373--374: paragraph beginning Using the study in Fujiwara, reduction to henselian I-valuative local rings, then to their valued residue fraction fields.

proof.text: Use the common limit topos, its colimit sheaves and exchange morphisms from [lem-per-admissible-modification-cohomology-presentation]. Apply [lem-per-admissible-modification-fujiwara-valuative-local] to select its conservative subfamily and, at a chosen point $t$, form the explicit local rings $B=B_t$, $C=B'_t$ and the local map $u:B\to C$. Write $IB=(\varphi)$ and $\varphi'=u(\varphi)$, so $IC=(\varphi')$. Both generators are nonunit nonzerodivisors. The same lemma supplies the $I$-valuative property, and the canonical formulas for the two stalks as cohomology on $S=B[1/\varphi]$ and $S'=C[1/\varphi']$. It also identifies the exchange map at this intermediate stage with pullback along $S\to S'$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.373: the limit topos and reduction to its henselian I-valuative local rings.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-admissible-modification-valuative-ring-reduction] separately to $(B,\varphi)$ and $(C,\varphi')$; its principal-ideal hypothesis and henselianity are exactly those obtained in Step 1. Set $P=\bigcap_n\varphi^nB$, $Q=\bigcap_n(\varphi')^nC$, $V=B/P$, $W=C/Q$, $K=\operatorname{Frac}(V)$ and $K'=\operatorname{Frac}(W)$. The lemma gives henselian valuation rings $V,W$, identifies $S/PS=K$ and $S'/QS'=K'$, and gives their valuation topologies with bases $\bar\varphi^nV$ and $(\bar\varphi')^nW$. In particular their fraction fields are henselian as valued fields, which by definition means that their valuation rings are henselian. Their valuations are nontrivial because $\bar\varphi$ and $\bar\varphi'$ are nonzero nonunits.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374: the henselian localization, intersection prime and valuation quotient.

proof.text: The congruence lemma [lem-per-admissible-modification-completion-density], applied to the corresponding blowups and the same geometric residue-field closures used in Step 1, gives $B/\varphi^nB\simeq C/(\varphi')^nC$ for every $n\geq1$. Thus $u^{-1}(Q)=P$: an element lies in the inverse image precisely when it is zero in every one of these quotients. Therefore $u$ induces an injection $V\hookrightarrow W$ and hence an inclusion $K\hookrightarrow K'$. Since $P\subseteq\varphi^nB$ and $Q\subseteq(\varphi')^nC$, the same quotient isomorphisms give $V/\bar\varphi^nV\simeq W/(\bar\varphi')^nW$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, final Note: congruences on the corresponding blowups.

proof.text: For $c\in W$ and $n\geq1$, the last quotient isomorphism supplies $b\in V$ with $c-b\in(\bar\varphi')^nW$. This proves that $V$ is dense in $W$. The same isomorphism says $V\cap(\bar\varphi')^nW=\bar\varphi^nV$, so it also identifies the induced topology. For a general $x'=c/(\bar\varphi')^r\in K'=W[1/\bar\varphi']$, approximate $c$ by $b\in V$ modulo $(\bar\varphi')^{n+r}W$; then $x'-b/\bar\varphi^r\in(\bar\varphi')^nW$. These balls, and their translates, form the field valuation topology by Step 2, so $K$ is dense in $K'$. Moreover $K\cap(\bar\varphi')^nW=\bar\varphi^nV$ for $n\geq1$: write an element of $K$ as $b/\bar\varphi^r$ and use $V\cap(\bar\varphi')^{n+r}W=\bar\varphi^{n+r}V$. This proves that the topology on $K$ is the induced topology. Set $K_t=K$ and $K'_t=K'$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374: passage from the common formal neighbourhoods to the dense valued-field embedding; elementary congruence argument written out.

proof.text: Let $E=F_t$ be the inverse image of $F$ on $\operatorname{Spec}S$, and let $E'$ be its inverse image on $\operatorname{Spec}S'$, as in Step 1. Define $G_t=i^{-1}E$ for the closed-point map $i:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}S$. Step 2 says $(S,PS)$ and $(S',QS')$ are henselian pairs, with residue fields $K,K'$. All these coefficient sheaves are torsion abelian, since inverse image preserves the local annihilation condition. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-gabber-pair-comparison] to these two pairs and $E,E'$: the canonical restriction maps give $H^q(S,E)\simeq H^q(K,G_t)$ and $H^q(S',E')\simeq H^q(K',(i')^{-1}E')$ for every $q\geq0$. Composing with the punctured-local formulas of Step 1 yields the required stalk identifications; the same sheaf $G_t$ works in every degree.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374: reduction from the punctured henselian local schemes to the fraction fields of the valuation quotients.

proof.text: The homomorphisms fit into the commutative square $S\to S'$, $S\to K$, $S'\to K'$, $K\to K'$: an element $b/\varphi^r$ has image $u(b)/(\varphi')^r$ on either path after passing to the quotients. Thus $(i')^{-1}E'$ is canonically the inverse image $G_t|_{K'}$. By the composition and coefficient-naturality assertions of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial], the resulting square of cohomology pullbacks commutes: $(i')^*u_S^*=u_K^*i^*$. Step 1 identifies the stalk exchange with $u_S^*$. Conjugating by the two restriction isomorphisms of Step 5 therefore gives exactly $u_K^*:H^q(K,G_t)\to H^q(K',G_t|_{K'})$. This proves the asserted exchange compatibility at each of the selected points. The family was already conservative in Step 1; no further inference from conservativity is needed.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374: canonical comparison maps, with compatibility verified by the square of ring homomorphisms.

proof_origin.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374; the final completion Note and XX 2.4.4, printed p.365.

Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair, with $I$ finitely generated, and let $A'=\widehat A$ be its $I$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, $U=X\setminus V(I)$, and define $X',Z',U'$ by base change to $A'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-base-change]. Let $F$ be a torsion abelian etale sheaf on $U$ and $F'$ its inverse image on $U'$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. For finitely generated ideals $J$ with $V(J)=V(I)$, form $B_J=\operatorname{Bl}_J(X)$, $Z_J=B_J\times_XZ$, and $j_J:U\hookrightarrow B_J$ [def-nagata-affine-blowup]. Order these blowups by domination, identifying ideals giving the same blowup. Their closed fibres form a cofiltered system. The limit of their small etale topoi, denoted $\mathcal T$, has a conservative family of geometric points (compatible geometric points of the closed fibres). Write $p_J:\mathcal T\to (Z_J)_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the projections and
$$L^q_F=\varinjlim_Jp_J^{-1}\bigl((R^qj_{J*}F)|_{Z_J}\bigr)\quad(q\geq0).$$
Here $R^qj_*$ is the higher direct image on abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and the transition maps are the natural pullback/exchange maps. There is a natural first-quadrant cohomological spectral sequence [def-sp-spectral-sequence]
$$E_2^{p,q}=H^p(\mathcal T,L^q_F)\ \Longrightarrow\ H^{p+q}(U_{\mathrm{et}},F).$$
Cohomology on a topos means the right derived functors of global sections, as for [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Convergence gives, in total degree $n\geq0$, a filtration with $n+1$ graded pieces $E_\infty^{p,n-p}$. Completion identifies $\mathcal T$ with the corresponding limit topos for $(A',IA')$, by the identifications of the closed fibres of corresponding admissible blowups; the blowups extended from $A$ are cofinal among those for $A'$. Under this identification the exchange maps induce a morphism $L^q_F\to L^q_{F'}$ and a morphism of the displayed spectral sequences. On their abutments it is the canonical pullback $H^n(U,F)\to H^n(U',F')$, including the specified filtrations. No isomorphism of the coefficient sheaves $L^q$ or of the abutments is asserted.

Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair with $I$ finitely generated, let $A'=\widehat A$ be its $I$-adic completion, and put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $U=X\setminus V(I)$ and $U'=\operatorname{Spec}A'\times_XU$ [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For each finitely generated ideal $J$ with $V(J)=V(I)$ write $Y_J=\operatorname{Bl}_J(X)$, and write $Y'_J$ for the corresponding blowup over $A'$ [def-nagata-affine-blowup]. Let $\mathcal T$ and $L^q_F,L^q_{F'}$ be the limit topos and colimit sheaves of [lem-per-admissible-modification-cohomology-presentation], for a torsion abelian etale sheaf $F$ on $U$ and its inverse image $F'$ on $U'$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. There is a conservative family of compatible geometric points $t=(\bar t_J)$ of the closed fibres for which the following holds. Form
$$B_t=\varinjlim_J\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y_J,\bar t_J},\qquad B'_t=\varinjlim_J\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y'_J,\bar t'_J}$$
using the compatible points on corresponding closed fibres and strict henselizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. These are nonzero henselian local rings, with the induced local map $u_t:B_t\to B'_t$. There is a nonunit nonzerodivisor $\varphi_t\in B_t$ such that $IB_t=(\varphi_t)$ and $IB'_t=(\varphi'_t)$ for $\varphi'_t=u_t(\varphi_t)$, also a nonunit nonzerodivisor. In each ring every finitely generated ideal containing a positive power of its displayed principal ideal is principal and generated by a nonzerodivisor; this is the $I$-valuative property used here. Put $S_t=B_t[1/\varphi_t]$, $S'_t=B'_t[1/\varphi'_t]$, and let $F_t$ be the inverse image of $F$ under $\operatorname{Spec}S_t\to U$, with $F'_t$ its inverse image on $\operatorname{Spec}S'_t$. There are canonical restriction isomorphisms, for every $q\geq0$,
$$(L^q_F)_t\simeq H^q((\operatorname{Spec}S_t)_{\mathrm{et}},F_t),\qquad (L^q_{F'})_t\simeq H^q((\operatorname{Spec}S'_t)_{\mathrm{et}},F'_t).$$
Under these isomorphisms the exchange morphism on stalks is the pullback induced by $S_t\to S'_t$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback].

Let $B$ be a nonzero commutative henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and let $\varphi\in B$ be a nonunit nonzerodivisor. Assume that every finitely generated ideal of $B$ containing $(\varphi^n)$ for some $n\geq1$ is principal and generated by a nonzerodivisor. Put $P=\bigcap_{n\geq1}\varphi^nB$, $S=B[1/\varphi]$, and $V=B/P$. Then $P$ is prime, $S$ is a henselian local ring with maximal ideal $PS$, and $V$ is a henselian valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring]. The canonical quotient map identifies
$$S/PS=V[1/\bar\varphi]=\operatorname{Frac}(V),$$
where $\bar\varphi$ is the image of $\varphi$ in $V$ and $\operatorname{Frac}(V)$ is its fraction field. Moreover $\bar\varphi$ is nonzero and noninvertible, and the ideals $\bar\varphi^nV$ form a neighbourhood basis of zero for the valuation topology, whose neighbourhoods are the sets $\{x:v(x)>\gamma\}$ for the additive valuation associated with $V$.

Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair with $I$ finitely generated and $A'=\widehat A$ its $I$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Set $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $X'=\operatorname{Spec}A'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For a finitely generated ideal $J\subseteq A$ with $V(J)=V(I)$ let $Y_J=\operatorname{Bl}_J(X)$ and $Y'_J=\operatorname{Bl}_{JA'}(X')$ [def-nagata-affine-blowup]. Then the canonical map induces isomorphisms of infinitesimal closed fibres
$$Y'_J\times_{X'}\operatorname{Spec}(A'/I^nA')\xrightarrow{\sim}Y_J\times_X\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^n)\quad(n\geq1).$$
Choose a compatible system $\bar t_J$ of geometric points on the closed fibres of the $Y_J$, and the corresponding system $\bar t'_J$ on the $Y'_J$, using the same separable residue-field closures. Define
$$B=\varinjlim_J\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y_J,\bar t_J},\qquad C=\varinjlim_J\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y'_J,\bar t'_J},$$
where the colimits use domination of blowups and strict henselizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. The induced homomorphism $u:B\to C$ gives isomorphisms $B/I^nB\xrightarrow{\sim}C/I^nC$ for all $n\geq1$. In particular, if $IB=(\varphi)$ and $\varphi'=u(\varphi)$, these are the maps $B/\varphi^nB\xrightarrow{\sim}C/(\varphi')^nC$.

Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ and $z:Z\to X$ the closed immersion. For every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] the pullback map [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]
$$
z^*:H^q(X_{\Et},F)\longrightarrow H^q(Z_{\Et},z^{-1}F)
$$
is an isomorphism for every $q\ge0$ ($H^q$ etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], $z^{-1}$ the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]). Only the pair form is asserted: for an affine scheme of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ in place of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ the comparison with the closed fibre is false (see the report of lemma-weil-pbc-injective-restriction-acyclicity and the Lean docstring of AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.bijective_cohomologyMap_of_henselianRing).

For each finitely generated ideal $J$ with $V(J)=V(I)$ write $Y_J=\operatorname{Bl}_J(X)$, and write $Y'_J$ for the corresponding blowup over $A'$ [def-nagata-affine-blowup]. Let $\mathcal T$ and $L^q_F,L^q_{F'}$ be the limit topos and colimit sheaves of [lem-per-admissible-modification-cohomology-presentation], for a torsion abelian etale sheaf $F$ on $U$ and its inverse image $F'$ on $U'$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. There is a conservative family of compatible geometric points $t=(\bar t_J)$ of the closed fibres for which the following holds. Form
$$B_t=\varinjlim_J\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y_J,\bar t_J},\qquad B'_t=\varinjlim_J\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y'_J,\bar t'_J}$$
using the compatible points on corresponding closed fibres and strict henselizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. These are nonzero henselian local rings, with the induced local map $u_t:B_t\to B'_t$. There is a nonunit nonzerodivisor $\varphi_t\in B_t$ such that $IB_t=(\varphi_t)$ and $IB'_t=(\varphi'_t)$ for $\varphi'_t=u_t(\varphi_t)$, also a nonunit nonzerodivisor. In each ring every finitely generated ideal containing a positive power of its displayed principal ideal is principal and generated by a nonzerodivisor; this is the $I$-valuative property used here. Put $S_t=B_t[1/\varphi_t]$, $S'_t=B'_t[1/\varphi'_t]$, and let $F_t$ be the inverse image of $F$ under $\operatorname{Spec}S_t\to U$, with $F'_t$ its inverse image on $\operatorname{Spec}S'_t$. There are canonical restriction isomorphisms, for every $q\geq0$,
$$(L^q_F)_t\simeq H^q((\operatorname{Spec}S_t)_{\mathrm{et}},F_t),\qquad (L^q_{F'})_t\simeq H^q((\operatorname{Spec}S'_t)_{\mathrm{et}},F'_t).$$
Under these isomorphisms the exchange morphism on stalks is the pullback induced by $S_t\to S'_t$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback].

Let $B$ be a nonzero commutative henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and let $\varphi\in B$ be a nonunit nonzerodivisor. Assume that every finitely generated ideal of $B$ containing $(\varphi^n)$ for some $n\geq1$ is principal and generated by a nonzerodivisor. Put $P=\bigcap_{n\geq1}\varphi^nB$, $S=B[1/\varphi]$, and $V=B/P$. Then $P$ is prime, $S$ is a henselian local ring with maximal ideal $PS$, and $V$ is a henselian valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring]. The canonical quotient map identifies
$$S/PS=V[1/\bar\varphi]=\operatorname{Frac}(V),$$
where $\bar\varphi$ is the image of $\varphi$ in $V$ and $\operatorname{Frac}(V)$ is its fraction field. Moreover $\bar\varphi$ is nonzero and noninvertible, and the ideals $\bar\varphi^nV$ form a neighbourhood basis of zero for the valuation topology, whose neighbourhoods are the sets $\{x:v(x)>\gamma\}$ for the additive valuation associated with $V$.

For a morphism of schemes $u:Y\to X$ [def-pc-scheme] and an abelian sheaf $G$ on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], let $u^*:H^q(X_{\Et},G)\to H^q(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}G)$ be the pullback map of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback], built from a K-injective resolution $s:G\to I^\bullet$ and a K-injective resolution $r:u^{-1}I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], as $\mathcal H^q$ of $a\mapsto r(\eta_u(a))$, $\eta_u$ the unit of $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For a morphism $\varphi:G\to G'$ of abelian sheaves on a scheme $T$ and K-injective resolutions $G\to I^\bullet$, $G'\to I'^\bullet$, write $H^q(\varphi):H^q(T_{\Et},G)\to H^q(T_{\Et},G')$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] for $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(T,\tilde\varphi))$, where $\tilde\varphi:I^\bullet\to I'^\bullet$ is any morphism of complexes with $\tilde\varphi\circ(G\to I^\bullet)$ homotopic to $(G'\to I'^\bullet)\circ\varphi$; such $\tilde\varphi$ exist and $H^q(\varphi)$ does not depend on $\tilde\varphi$ (step 1), and for $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_G$ these are the identifications of the groups computed from different resolutions [prop-weil-pbc-cohomology-resolution-independent]. Then:

1. (Independence.) $u^*$ does not depend on the choice of $I^\bullet$ and $J^\bullet$: for a second choice $(I'^\bullet,J'^\bullet)$ the two maps $u^*$ agree after the identifications $H^q(\mathrm{id}_G)$ and $H^q(\mathrm{id}_{u^{-1}G})$. The same holds for $u^*:\RGamma(X_{\Et},K)\to\RGamma(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}K)$, $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], as a morphism of $\Dplus(\Ab)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] up to the canonical isomorphisms between the complexes computed from different resolutions.
2. (Any comparison complex.) Let $t:u^{-1}G\to M^\bullet$ be a quasi-isomorphism to a bounded below complex of abelian sheaves on $Y_{\Et}$ and $\beta:u^{-1}I^\bullet\to M^\bullet$ a morphism of complexes with $\beta\circ u^{-1}(s)=t$. Let $\gamma:M^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ be a morphism of complexes with $\gamma\circ t$ homotopic to $r\circ u^{-1}(s)$ (it exists, unique up to homotopy). Then $u^*=\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(Y,\gamma))\circ\mathcal H^q\bigl(a\mapsto\beta(\eta_u(a))\bigr)$, the second map being $\mathcal H^q$ of $\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)\to\Gamma(Y,M^\bullet)$. If $M^\bullet$ is K-injective, or a complex of $\Gamma(Y,-)$-acyclic sheaves, then $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(Y,\gamma))$ is an isomorphism, so that $u^*$ is computed on $\Gamma(Y,M^\bullet)$ by $a\mapsto\beta(\eta_u(a))$.
3. (Naturality.) For a morphism $\varphi:G\to G'$ of abelian sheaves on $X_{\Et}$, $u^*\circ H^q(\varphi)=H^q(u^{-1}\varphi)\circ u^*$.
4. (Composition.) For a morphism $v:Z\to Y$, let $c_{u,v}:v^{-1}u^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(u\circ v)^{-1}$ be the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (compatible with the units). Then $(u\circ v)^*=H^q(c_{u,v,G})\circ v^*\circ u^*:H^q(X_{\Et},G)\to H^q(Z_{\Et},(u\circ v)^{-1}G)$, and, with $e_X:\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ of the same lemma, $H^q(e_{X,G})\circ\mathrm{id}_X^*=\mathrm{id}$.
5. (Etale maps.) If $u$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], let $\rho_G:u^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}G|_Y$ be the identification of the inverse image with the restriction, $G|_Y(V)=G(V)$ for $V$ etale over $Y$, of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]. If $G\to I^\bullet$ is a resolution by a bounded below complex of injective abelian sheaves, then $u^{-1}G\to u^{-1}I^\bullet$ is a resolution of $u^{-1}G$ by a bounded below complex of injective abelian sheaves, one may take $J^\bullet=u^{-1}I^\bullet$, $r=\mathrm{id}$, and then $u^*$ is $\mathcal H^q$ of the restriction map $\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)=I^\bullet(X)\to I^\bullet(Y)\cong\Gamma(Y,u^{-1}I^\bullet)$ (through $\rho_{I^\bullet}(Y)$) along $u:Y\to X$.

Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair with $I$ finitely generated, let $A'=\widehat A$ be its $I$-adic completion, and put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $U=X\setminus V(I)$ and $U'=\operatorname{Spec}A'\times_XU$ [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For each finitely generated ideal $J$ with $V(J)=V(I)$ write $Y_J=\operatorname{Bl}_J(X)$, and write $Y'_J$ for the corresponding blowup over $A'$ [def-nagata-affine-blowup]. Let $\mathcal T$ and $L^q_F,L^q_{F'}$ be the limit topos and colimit sheaves of [lem-per-admissible-modification-cohomology-presentation], for a torsion abelian etale sheaf $F$ on $U$ and its inverse image $F'$ on $U'$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. There is a conservative family of compatible geometric points $t=(\bar t_J)$ of the closed fibres for which the following holds. Form
$$B_t=\varinjlim_J\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y_J,\bar t_J},\qquad B'_t=\varinjlim_J\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y'_J,\bar t'_J}$$
using the compatible points on corresponding closed fibres and strict henselizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. These are nonzero henselian local rings, with the induced local map $u_t:B_t\to B'_t$. There is a nonunit nonzerodivisor $\varphi_t\in B_t$ such that $IB_t=(\varphi_t)$ and $IB'_t=(\varphi'_t)$ for $\varphi'_t=u_t(\varphi_t)$, also a nonunit nonzerodivisor. In each ring every finitely generated ideal containing a positive power of its displayed principal ideal is principal and generated by a nonzerodivisor; this is the $I$-valuative property used here. Put $S_t=B_t[1/\varphi_t]$, $S'_t=B'_t[1/\varphi'_t]$, and let $F_t$ be the inverse image of $F$ under $\operatorname{Spec}S_t\to U$, with $F'_t$ its inverse image on $\operatorname{Spec}S'_t$. There are canonical restriction isomorphisms, for every $q\geq0$,
$$(L^q_F)_t\simeq H^q((\operatorname{Spec}S_t)_{\mathrm{et}},F_t),\qquad (L^q_{F'})_t\simeq H^q((\operatorname{Spec}S'_t)_{\mathrm{et}},F'_t).$$
Under these isomorphisms the exchange morphism on stalks is the pullback induced by $S_t\to S'_t$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback].

Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ and $z:Z\to X$ the closed immersion. For every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] the pullback map [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]
$$
z^*:H^q(X_{\Et},F)\longrightarrow H^q(Z_{\Et},z^{-1}F)
$$
is an isomorphism for every $q\ge0$ ($H^q$ etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], $z^{-1}$ the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]). Only the pair form is asserted: for an affine scheme of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ in place of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ the comparison with the closed fibre is false (see the report of lemma-weil-pbc-injective-restriction-acyclicity and the Lean docstring of AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.bijective_cohomologyMap_of_henselianRing).
